title: Argosy Inc - Postmortem & Mitigation Plan
summary: Follow-up to the Mar 18 production outage impacting Redwood Dedicated pool for Argosy. Reviewed timeline, root cause (autoscaler race + KV cache eviction + model OOM under spike), short and long-term mitigations, monitoring gaps, and next steps including patch, bench tests, and a joint runbook. Argosy requested timeline for fixes and temporary workarounds and asked for credit discussion; Redwood committed to sending postmortem doc, security artefacts, and a schedule for load testing.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration 55m | Attendees: Tom (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Jordan (SRE), Maya (Argosy SRE), Carlos (Argosy Eng Mgr), Nora (Argosy Security), Ethan (Argosy Platform), Olivia (Product)

[00:00] Tom (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, sorry we had to reschedule earlier, um this is the postmortem follow-up for the incident on the 18th that affected your dedicated pool. We want to walk through timeline, RCA, and get alignment on mitigations and next steps.

[00:25] Carlos (Argosy): Thanks Tom, quick call out from our side — the spike impacted checkout flows at 14:12 UTC and we saw error rates spike to ~18% for 8 minutes, so it's pretty visible. We're hoping for an action plan and timeline.

[00:48] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah hi all, I'm Priya, I'll run the technical bits. Quick TL;DR: root cause was an autoscaler race where two scale-down and scale-up ops raced under load, combined with an aggressive KV cache eviction policy that caused cold-starty stalls on models with large KV caches. That in turn pushed some GPU workers into OOMs when sequence lengths spiked — so a cascade.

[01:12] Maya (Argosy): When you say "race", do you mean the controller issued conflicting decisions?

[01:20] Priya: Exactly — controller A observed low utilization then triggered scale-down, controller B later saw queue backlog and tried to scale up but the scale-down had progressed and a bunch of workers were deprovisioned. During the transient the routing layer fell back to a smaller set of instances and the KV cache misses spiked — the model runtime then did aggressive rehydration causing memory pressure. The short: all three factors together.

[02:04] Ethan (Argosy): Could this have been prevented by pinning the model version or disabling autoscale during the rollout?

[02:12] Tom: Good question; as a short-term customer workaround we recommended pinning to the previous model variant and setting a minimum node count on the dedicated pool. We documented this in the support note we shared.

[02:36] Nora (Argosy Security): Was there any data exfil or integrity concern? Our security needs that first.

[02:44] Jordan (Redwood SRE): No signs of exfil, all accesses were internal control plane events. We'll include audit logs and request traces in the security appendix. We'll also provide KMS logs as requested.

[03:10] Carlos: Ok great, makes sense. Can you walk through the minute-by-minute timeline?

[03:18] Priya: Sure — quick timeline: 14:08 normal throughput; 14:11 traffic spike due to marketing campaign; 14:12 queue backlog starts; 14:13 autoscaler A triggers scale-down (incorrectly due to a stale metric window); 14:14 several workers drain; 14:15 autoscaler B triggers scale-up; 14:16 routing imbalance causes KV cache misses, rehydrations begin; 14:17–14:20 memory pressure leads to model OOMs and elevated 5xx errors; 14:21 fallback policy routed some requests to a non-optimal variant causing higher latency until load subsided at 14:26.

[04:05] Maya: Those timestamps align with what we saw. Do you have logs we can correlate?

[04:12] Tom: We'll share the consolidated trace bundle and a condensed timeline CSV. The bundle will be in the postmortem attachment.

[04:28] Olivia (Product): From a customer impact POV we'd like to know expected recurrence probability and what changes reduce that to near zero.

[04:36] Priya: We'll break mitigations into short-term, medium, and long-term. Short-term (hours–days): 1) Set min_nodes on pools, 2) disable overly aggressive cache eviction by bumping thresholds, 3) apply routing fallback tighter to avoid falling back to incompatible variants. Medium-term (1–3 weeks): patch autoscaler metric window + add leader election to avoid dual controllers, strengthen cache metrics, and add pre-warm on scale events. Long-term (1–3 months): architectural changes to isolate KV cache per worker group, improve kernel-level memory handling, and more sophisticated predictive autoscaling.

[05:30] Ethan: The pre-warm sounds critical — what's involved?

[05:36] Priya: Pre-warm is a short burst that instantiates empty model state then runs a few warmup requests so KV caches are populated before traffic lands. We'll make it optional per pool and automated based on traffic signals.

[05:58] Carlos: On the timeline, is the autoscaler fix just a config change or code?

[06:04] Priya: It's code — we need to adjust the metric smoothing and add leader election logic in the controller to prevent simultaneous opposing actions. We can also add a short coordination window as a patch. We'll open a PR and share details.

[06:20] Jordan (Redwood): We already have a candidate patch that reduces the smoothing timeslice and adds a lightweight lock. Priya will shepherd the PR.

[06:32] Nora: From security — we'll need the audit log export and confirmation there were no ambiguous IAM events.

[06:38] Tom: Understood — we'll add an appendix with CloudTrail-like activity and the KMS access logs.

[06:50] Maya: On monitoring, we noticed no alert fired for KV cache miss rate. Can we add that?

[06:58] Priya: Yes that's an explicit gap. We'll add a KV cache miss-rate metric and an SLO-based alert. Also increase retention for eviction histograms for 30 days.

[07:18] Liam (CSM): Customer communication — Argosy requested a status page update and an email to engineering leads with the postmortem link once it's ready. We'll coordinate that.

[07:32] Carlos: Also we need a runbook for manual scale-up fallback if autoscale exhibits anomalies.

[07:38] Jordan (Redwood): We'll provide a runbook and we can also enable an operator action in the console for manual override.

[07:48] Olivia: About credits — what's Redwood's typical approach for a single outage of this length?

[07:56] Tom: We'll run this through finance; typical practice is to assess the SLA window impact and propose a credit. We'll share a proposal by end of next week.

[08:10] Nora: Will you include any security review changes in that proposal?

[08:15] Tom: Security artifacts are separate; we'll send those immediately and they won't be contingent on finance.

[08:24] Maya: For the joint load test — we want to replay the production traffic spike with seq length and burst patterns. What's the expected duration?

[08:32] Priya: Plan for 2 hours including setup and cooldown; we'll coordinate a 2-hour window and do a dry run. Jordan will schedule.

[08:46] Ethan: A logistical question — will this test run on Argosy's Dedicated pool or a mirror?

[08:52] Priya: Prefer doing it on a mirror to avoid risk to production, but we can do a controlled run on a non-prod dedicated pool that mirrors your config. Argosy decide which.

[09:06] Carlos: We'll share the sandbox access details and workload replay by Tue.

[09:12] Tom: Great. Any other blockers?

[09:15] Maya: Just one — can you add a specific metric to detect controller split-brain earlier? That would help.

[09:22] Priya: Yep we'll add a controller-leader-latency metric and alert if there's an overlap in leader token holders.

[09:34] Liam: After we implement the short-term mitigations, we'll run a 24–48 hour monitoring window and then reconvene. Proposed follow-up meeting: Mar 27 to review test results and PR status.

[09:48] Carlos: Mar 27 works.

[09:52] Tom: Ok I'll send calendar invite. We'll share the postmortem doc by Monday and PR links as they open.

[10:00] Priya: Quick note on the model variant fallback — we recommend adding compatibility metadata on variants so routing can quickly choose compatible ones if fallback needed. We'll propose a schema change.

[10:22] Nora: Please include that in the design appendix. Security will review.

[10:30] Tom: Recap of action items and owners — we'll paste these in the calendar note and in the ticket. Thanks everyone.

[10:40] Carlos: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

[10:48] End of transcript.

References: postmortem draft (link: https://redwood.dev/pm/ARG-2026-03-18), load test plan (sheet link: https://sheets.redwood.dev/argosy-loadtest), security appendix (link: https://redwood.dev/security/argosy-2026)
